trigger.details: Routine complexity-escalation check per the skill's five-metric table (cyclomatic complexity per method, afferent coupling per module, fan-in/fan-out ratio, regulatory surface area, zero-coverage+high-churn). All five metrics were computed directly against both modules (gildedrose-console, gildedrose-tests) and none exceeded threshold: cyclomatic complexity max ~17 (UpdateQuality, Program.cs:37-111) vs >50; afferent coupling 0 vs >8 (single-solution, no internal_dependencies per structural-analysis.json); fan-in/fan-out not applicable (zero internal edges); regulatory surface area none found (no PII/financial/safety-critical path, structural-analysis.json integration_points: []); zero coverage (proven, see quality-risk.json test_coverage) but churn is unmeasurable/effectively nil (single-commit repository history, no remote configured). This record is filed for audit-trail completeness per the output contract, not because a threshold breach occurred (see quality-risk.md §6 for the full per-metric table).

resolution.description: No complexity-escalation threshold was exceeded by either module in this application; the check itself, its inputs, and its per-metric results are recorded here as an auditable disposition rather than a silent omission, per the skill's escalation methodology. Separately, this assessment also carries forward (in quality-risk.json risk_summary.top_risk_drivers and quality-risk.md §0) an unresolved governing-profile/application-identity discrepancy — the source tree is the generic public 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata' with a conflicting DSHS assembly-metadata attribution, while the FAA profile governs this task's execution per binding instruction — which is a non-blocking open question for a stakeholder to confirm, not a complexity-escalation trigger, so it does not change this record's severity or status.

review_asks.assessment: None of the five complexity-escalation metrics (cyclomatic complexity >50, afferent coupling >8, fan-in/fan-out >5:1, regulatory surface area, zero-coverage+high-churn) was exceeded by either gildedrose-console or gildedrose-tests. This does not soften the pass's overall HIGH risk tier, which rests on proven zero test coverage, an unseamed 75-line rules engine, an EOL .NET Framework runtime, and a non-hermetic build chain — none of which maps onto this specific five-metric escalation table.

Zero coverage + high churn: coverage is 0% (structurally proven — GildedRose.Tests.csproj declares no <ProjectReference> to GildedRose.Console), but churn is unmeasurable because the repository's entire history is a single commit with no remote configured, so the conjunctive high-churn condition cannot be met.
